entry.description: A repaired combinatorial double-sieve inequality in Wu2008 and Li2024. The primary source reports: The source reports repairing the last triple-sum range in Wu2008 Lemma2.2 and Li2024 Lemma3.1 to N^kappa2<=p4<N^(1/2−3kappa1), with the stated sieve-set corrections and explicit error4N/(N^kappa1−1) for A={N−p}. The resulting finite-count inequality holds for every N>1 under the listed admissibility hypotheses. The analytic sieve evaluations and downstream0.899 constant are not proved or corrected here. Direct AI connection: Steve Hubbard explicitly states that a ClaudeOpus5.5 agent found the gap while formalizing, wrote the repaired statement and all Lean code, with human publication direction and separate AI statement auditors. Further checking: Ask the original authors or an independent sieve specialist to check the altered range, sifted sets, error and weakened boundary hypothesis. The printed pointwise-counterexample test is outside this selected proof closure; do not infer a disproof of the final Goldbach or Chen bounds. No human expert review or independent artifact replay is claimed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Lenses make many points: pure point spectrum disproves Simon’s L² conjecture. The primary source reports: For every d>=2 and0<=sigma<1/3, the authors construct a smooth bounded nonnegative potential V with arbitrarily small ||V||_infinity+integral |x|^(1−d+sigma)|V|², for which −Delta+V has only pure point spectrum on(0,infinity). This contradicts Simon’s stated weighted-L² absolutely-continuous-spectrum conjecture. Direct AI connection: Becker and Yang describe developing the initial construction with ChatGPT, which supplied the point-spectrum parameter adjustment, spectral averaging and extension from a bounded interval to the full positive spectrum; humans rewrote and checked the argument. Further checking: Independently check the lens and higher-dimensional construction, weighted norm, spectral averaging and the exact positive-energy meaning. Human responsibility and rewriting are not independent end-to-end proof verification. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: The Critical 2D KPZ Process. The primary source reports: The paper constructs a non-Gaussian distribution-valued critical2D KPZ process as the unique limit in law of centered log partition functions of critical two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers, and as a measurable renormalized Cole–Hopf function of the Critical2D Stochastic Heat Flow. It reports log-log covariance blow-up and small-scale Gaussian fluctuations. This is not universality for every microscopic KPZ model. Direct AI connection: The eleven authors disclose extensive ChatGPT5.5/5.6/6 contributions to tightness, convergence to a unique limit and non-Gaussianity, within human-supplied strategies and a decade-long research programme; AppendixC also records failed AI approaches and subsequent corrections. Further checking: Audit tightness, centering, uniqueness of the limiting law, SHF measurability and non-Gaussianity, including the failed intermediate strategies described in AppendixC. Do not extend Gaussian-polymer hypotheses to an unrestricted universality theorem. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Generalized Boyd constructions of small-Mahler-measure polynomials. The primary source reports: The paper gives a five-parameter Generalized Boyd construction with a cyclotomic-free choice for every even degree d>=12 and reports exactly verified irreducible polynomials with Mahler measure below alpha1≈1.255434 for every even d in[12,2000]. The search improves six published values and attains99.6% of the reported records in that finite range. It does not resolve Lehmer’s problem. Direct AI connection: Chervonyi, Gukov and Luong describe a human–AI discovery loop using internal Gemini models including Gemini4Argon in Google Antigravity, which built numerical/symbolic search infrastructure, distributed searches and analytical conjecture extraction. Further checking: Separate the general cyclotomic-free degree construction from the finite verified measure sweep. Independently check irreducibility certificates, degree conventions, parameter bounds, alpha1 comparison and baseline-record ownership. Do not infer a universal Mahler gap or a disproof of Lehmer. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

Further checking: Check degeneracy normalization, the boundary blow-up and ellipticity hypotheses, and novelty relative to the Monge–Ampère and prior k-Hessian cases. This does not cover arbitrary nonconvex domains. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Sharp lower bounds for Steklov decay on curvilinear polygons. The primary source reports: For the paper’s single-corner domains Omega_alpha and alpha in(0,2pi) outside its exceptional-angle set E, the harmonic Steklov extensions have a positive limsup after multiplication by sigma_j^(pi/alpha) on every interior ball. Moving one of two small isometric holes yields a positive spectral-difference limsup at order sigma_j^(−2pi/alpha), proving the stated earlier error exponents sharp. Direct AI connection: Galkowski and Wang attribute the regularized-trace and corner-kernel proof ideas to ChatGPT6Astra; humans supplied the domain construction, conformal simplification and small-angle method. Further checking: Audit the exceptional-angle set, normalizations, limsup versus all-eigenfunction quantifiers, hole-size hypotheses and local-boundary-information comparison. Do not claim all curvilinear polygons or every angle satisfy this lower bound. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Local-height asymptotics without the Hodge-conjecture hypothesis. The primary source reports: For the stated flat projective family over a smooth complex curve, with smooth total space and generically disjoint complementary cycles homologically trivial on general fibers, the Archimedean height minus the local intersection index times log|t| extends continuously across the degeneration. The Hodge conjecture and the earlier additional intersection/semistability assumptions are not needed for this theorem. This does not prove the Hodge conjecture. Direct AI connection: Nakayama explicitly attributes the argument outline and identification of Scholl’s p-adic analogue to ChatGPT6Astra; the author supplied the remaining details and wrote the manuscript. Further checking: Audit the cohomological comparison, sign conventions, monodromy passage and precise cycle/family hypotheses against Theorem4.1 and the earlier conditional theorem. No independent expert review or proof artifact replay was found; do not generalize removal of one theorem’s Hodge assumption into a solution of Hodge. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Robust absorption for typed triangle decompositions. The primary source reports: The paper reports typical-host triangle decomposition theorems for admissible four-label families, including a finite-census theorem, their nearly complete/balanced consequences with explicit type weights, a semidense two-label mixed-triangle case, and a terminal absorber under bounded signed certificates and physical hinge supply. It retains typicality, local/global divisibility, extension and non-extremality hypotheses; arbitrary divisible hosts are not covered. Direct AI connection: The author’s pinned disclosure directly credits Aristotle, Claude and ChatGPT/Codex with mathematical exploration, counterexample search and proof development, not just formal translation; the author directed scope and research. Further checking: Check the765-family census, seventeen conserved families, ordered versus unordered normalization and physical hinge budgets. Compare combined statements with prior labelled-complex work and PaperI. Source-reported local/archived checks and an agent review are not independent human verification or replay here; priority remains provisional. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Retain provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description: Group constructions cannot refute the Set Cover Conjecture, including tensor powers. The primary source reports: Pratt (STOC 2024, arXiv:2311.02774, Corollary 1.12) showed that if the Set Cover Conjecture holds, then for every k the asymptotic rank of the balanced tripartitioning tensor T_k is at least tau_k = 8^k * C(3k,k) * C(2k,k) / 27^k. A natural way to bound this rank, and Pratt's own route to rank at most 8^k/2, is a group construction: maps f1, f2, f3 from k-subsets of a 3k-set to a group G with f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = 1 exactly when A, B, C are pairwise disjoint (a partition analogue of the Cohn-Umans triple product property). We formalise that no such construction, in any finite group, abelian or not, can refute the conjecture: |G| > tau_k for every k >= 2. The same holds for Strassen combinatorial degenerations of group tensors (border-rank constructions), via |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2)) > tau_k. The proof formalises a rigidity theorem: the triple products always factor through pairwise commuting elements, f1(A) f2(B) f3(C) = prod_i g_i^(m_i - 1) with m the multiplicity vector, so non-abelian groups give no advantage, unlike in the Cohn-Umans approach to matrix multiplication. It also formalises a lift lemma giving |G| >= 2^(3k-1), which shows Pratt's 8^k/2 is exactly optimal among group restrictions. Pratt's Corollary 1.12 and the passage from a group embedding to a rank bound are cited, not formalised. The bounds concern the group size needed by such constructions, not the rank of T_k itself. Joint constructions for tensor powers are covered: a degeneration of a group tensor onto T_k^(tensor m) needs |G| >= C(3k, floor(3k/2))^m > tau_k^m, so the induced asymptotic-rank bound |G|^(1/m) stays above tau_k. entry.description: Deterministic factoring in time N^{o(1)}. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 proof, against Mathlib, that one deterministic Turing machine computes the smallest prime factor Nat.minFac N of every natural number N in time N^{o(1)}: for every k >= 1 there is a constant C_k such that the same machine halts with the correct output within C_k * 2^(n/k) steps on every n-bit input. The machine model is Mathlib's Turing machine model TM2 (Turing.FinTM2 with Turing.TM2ComputableInTime), with numbers in binary (Computability.encodeNat) and every stack alphabet finite. The best previously published deterministic bounds known to the authors have exponent 1/5 (Harvey 2021; Harvey and Hittmeir 2022). The proof reduces finding the smallest prime factor to counting divisors with prescribed leading bits, expresses that count as the value of a network of local checks carrying out Schoenhage-Strassen multiplication, and evaluates it with a re-proved form of the counting engine of the 2026 3-SAT preprint by Claude (Anthropic). The Challenge also states, as a proposition only and without proof, a conjecture that factoring can be done in time exp(O(log N / sqrt(log log N))). The ideas and the Lean code were generated by AI; the authors audited the statement, not the proof. Direct AI involvement: AI-generated. entry.description: Weak and strong βη-normalization in pure type systems with βη-conversion. The primary source reports: A Lean formalization of the Barendregt-Geuvers-Klop conjecture, "weak normalization implies strong normalization", for the pure type systems PTS_βη of Geuvers (Logics and Type Systems, 1993), whose conversion rule uses βη-conversion. For every PTS specification, with no functionality assumption, it proves two theorems about the legal terms of PTS_βη. If every legal term is weakly βη-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. If every legal term is weakly β-normalizing, then every legal term is strongly βη-normalizing. The proof adapts OpenAI's 2026 proof of the β case for PTS_β, whose Lean files are included. An η-step can delete a λ-annotation, so the proof works from a weaker hypothesis, that every legal term has a β-reduct with no β-redex outside its λ-domains. Conversion is handled through domain erasure, candidates are indexed by βη-normal forms of erased types, and observation values are made η-canonical. Direct AI involvement:  Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) in Claude Code, with shell, Lean/Lake and file-editing tools, under the direction of the human authors. It adapted the proof to βη and wrote all the Lean code except OpenAI's 33 files in PTSBetaEta/Beta. It also ported those files to the Lean module system. entry.description: The critical Almost Stacked Hypothesis fails on a nine-vertex graph. The primary source reports: In graph pebbling, a move removes two pebbles from a vertex and adds one to a neighbour; a configuration is stackable if moves can bring all pebbles onto one vertex and clearable if moves can leave exactly one pebble. The stacking (clearing) number of a connected (connected non-bipartite) graph is the least t >= 2 such that every configuration of t pebbles is stackable (clearable). The Almost Stacked Hypothesis, in its critical form, says that this number equals the least t0 >= 2 such that every almost stacked configuration (one vertex arbitrary, every other vertex at most one pebble) of every size at least t0 is stackable (clearable). We formalise a counterexample to both clauses: on the nine-vertex graph G9 (graph6 HCQTaXi) the stacking and clearing numbers are 15, the only non-stackable and non-clearable configurations of size 14 are (0,0,1,0,0,5,0,8,0) and its automorphic image, neither almost stacked, while every almost stacked configuration of size at least 14 is stackable and clearable. Hence neither clause holds for all finite connected (respectively connected non-bipartite) graphs. The finite facts are proved by kernel evaluation (decide +kernel) of a verified exact losing-layer checker on certificate data; general lemmas (clearable implies stackable; monotonicity above the order) are proved by hand. entry.description: A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers: proof, equality cases and weighted forms. The primary source reports: For a vector v with nonnegative entries and a real number p, write v^p for the vector of p-th powers of its entries. Johnston, Plosker, Torrance and Varona (arXiv:2507.10327, Conjecture 5.1) conjectured that ‖v^p‖ ‖w^p‖ - ⟨v^p, w^p⟩ ≤ ‖v‖^p ‖w‖^p - ⟨v, w⟩^p for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors v, w in ℝⁿ with positive entries, with the Euclidean norm and inner product. They proved it for integer p and showed that it fails for 1 < p < 2. This formalization proves the conjecture for every real p ≥ 2 and all vectors with nonnegative entries. It also determines every case of equality: for p > 2 equality holds exactly when v and w are linearly dependent or each has at most one nonzero entry, and for p = 2 there is one further family supported on two coordinates. Finally, for positive coordinate weights ω used in every norm and inner product, the weighted inequality holds for all nonnegative vectors exactly when ω_i ω_j ≥ 1 for all i ≠ j, a condition that does not depend on p. The proof shows that a 2 × 2 entrywise-power defect matrix is positive semidefinite, using a double integral formula and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for integrals. The conjecture and its equality cases were also proved, independently and concurrently, by Johnston and Sababheh (arXiv:2610.12063). Direct AI involvement: The problem was chosen by the author from the Principia Math problem list. The first informal proof of the main inequality came from the Principia Math automated system. The author then used Claude through Claude Code to find and prove the equality cases and the weighted characterisation and to write the whole Lean development. The author checked the mathematics, read the statements in Challenge.lean against the paper, and is responsible for the content. No AI system is listed as an author. Finally, for positive coordinate weights ω used in every norm and inner product, the weighted inequality holds for all nonnegative vectors exactly when ω_i ω_j ≥ 1 for all i ≠ j, a condition that does not depend on p. entry.description: Erdős Problem 699: every counterexample has n ≤ j². The primary source reports: Erdős Problem 699 (Erdős and Szekeres 1978) asks whether for every 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n/2 there is a prime p ≥ i dividing gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)). The problem is open. Using the statement from google-deepmind/formal-conjectures with the single extra hypothesis j² < n, this project proves in Lean 4 with Mathlib that the answer is yes whenever j² < n; equivalently, every counterexample (n, i, j) has n ≤ j². The proof combines the Erdős–Szekeres inequality gcd(C(n, i), C(n, j)) ≥ C(n, i)/C(j, i) ≥ (n/j)^i, which follows from the identity C(n, j) C(j, i) = C(n, i) C(n − i, j − i), with an upper bound for a gcd whose prime factors are all below i: each prime power in C(n, i) is at most n (Kummer), and there are at most i/2 primes below i, so such a gcd is at most n^(i/2). The bound reduces the problem to j ≥ √n. With a computer search of every n < 10^12 (not part of this formalization) it rules out counterexamples with j ≤ 10^6. The argument is short and may well be folklore; formal-conjectures records the problem but no partial result of this kind. entry.description: BandParity: the band-parity sum of a quartic character, two laws modulo 4. The primary source reports: For a prime p = 5 (mod 8) let chi be the quartic Dirichlet character with chi(2) = i, with values in the Gaussian integers, and let C(p) = f + i e be the sum of chi(n) (-1)^floor(n^2/p) over 0 < n < p/2. The development proves that f = (p-1)/4 (mod 4) and e = kappa (mod 4) for every such p, where kappa is the sum of the Legendre symbols (n/p) over 0 < n < p/4. The mechanism is a matching lemma: for sign functions sigma, tau and a bijection pi, the correlation sum sigma(x) tau(pi x) is congruent modulo 4 to the sum of the two marginals minus the number of terms, so it does not depend on pi. Along the way it proves the parity dictionary (-1)^floor(n^2/p) = s(n) s(n^2) with s(x) = (-1)^<x>, the coset form f = sum over the fourth powers H of s(u) s(u^2) and e = the same sum over 2H, the lag identity sum over 2H of s(u) s(2u) = kappa exactly, the exact coset parities sum_H s = k + 2t and sum_{2H} s = t - 2k where B_{1,chi} = k + i t, and the Coordinate Congruence kappa = (p-1)/4 + k + t (mod 4). It also proves the odd-subgroup congruence: for an odd modulus N >= 3, a subgroup H of (Z/N)^x of odd order h, a coset X = xH and an even exponent e >= 2, the band-parity sum of X and -X over (0, N/2) equals sum over X of s(u) s(u^e) and is congruent to h - 2 alpha(X) - 2 alpha(X^e) modulo 4, where alpha counts elements with odd least residue. entry.description: Bounds for the iteration x ↦ a mod x. The primary source reports: For integers 0 < b < a, let P(a,b) count the positive terms obtained by repeatedly replacing x by a mod x, starting at b. This development proves the uniform bound P(a,b) ≤ C_ε a^((41301 - 3 sqrt(82849))/137480 + ε) for every ε > 0, including the external coefficient-uniform affine-curve theorem and the effective Hilbert specialisation sieve, and its rational instance 4317/14677. It also proves the exterior-lattice exponents 471/1559 - 6 sqrt(105)/7795 and 153/520, the joint-invariant exponents (1310-sqrt(655))/4365, 2201/7480 and 128/435 and the earlier exponents 45/152, 8/27, 11/37, 23/77, and 3/10. It also proves a bound O(a^(1/4) sqrt R), where R minus one counts rises in the quotient increments, and positivity and integrality of the orbit's Hankel invariants. A separate conditional theorem gives O(a^(3/10) sqrt(log log(3a))) assuming two explicitly stated analytic estimates whose proofs are not formalised. The polar bound uses the proved orbit identity, actual common-base bound of four, degree-twelve residue labels, uniform arithmetic specialisation count, and full-pattern completion count with arbitrary common divisors. entry.description: Proofs and corrections of OEIS conjectures. The primary source reports: Machine-checked proofs of conjectures recorded in 29 entries of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), together with corrections of the four conjectured statements that turn out to be false. Most of the sequences are coefficients of formal power series defined by functional equations, and most of the results describe their residues modulo small integers. The results form six families and a group of further results: the equation A(x*A - m*x*A^2) = x^2 (parity, residues modulo m^2, binary-digit divisibility and prime exponents for every m, with corrected residue classifications modulo 9 and 16 for A396843 and A396844); consecutive iterates F = x + F^{o r}*F^{o(r+1)} (every integer iterate modulo 2r, A396099, A396798, A396807); scaled inverses A(x - x*A(qx)/q) = x (every coefficient is 1 modulo q+1, and for even q the odd coefficients are exactly at the powers of 2, A393856-A393859); theta-series substitutions and theta-type sums (square patterns modulo 4, corrected for A380680, and a congruence modulo 16 for A355872); Catalan-type equations (residues modulo 2, 4 and 8 governed by powers of 2, A393172, A393171, A389536, A397588, A195194); equations with an exact halving step (residues modulo 4, 9 and 3, A389537, A389542, A389474, A389475); and further results on A396093, A392210, A396102 and its family F^{o r} = (1+x)*F^{o(r-1)}, A380056, A397346 and the greedy sequence A394576. Each family has its own Comparator configuration, and each OEIS entry has a self-contained paper in the repository. Direct AI involvement: Dev D. Goyal directed the project, chose the problems, requested proofs, formal verification and revisions, and reviewed the results, but did not supply proof strategies. entry.description: Chain returns and lower bounds for superpermutations. The primary source reports: Prove explicit general lower bounds for the shortest superpermutation length S(n), valid for every n >= 8. The exact-order and quadratic-order formulas refine the lower-order terms while retaining leading correction (2+o(1))(n-4)! above n!+(n-1)!+(n-2)!. The development also proves asymptotic comparisons with earlier general formulas; the selected theorem statements specify their exact scope. Separate finite refinements prove S(10) >= 4033379 and S(14) >= 93891141150. entry.description: The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete: point-point, boundary-point and point-boundary variants, in Lean 4. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow, "The Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete" (J. ACM 2021), together with Stade's point-boundary variant (SoCG 2025), for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model. Lean proves that deciding whether a simple polygon with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions in each of the three variants known to be ∃ℝ-complete: point guards guarding the whole polygon (Theorem 1, also for integer corners), guards on the boundary guarding the whole polygon (the boundary-point variant of the paper's §7.2), and point guards guarding only the boundary (Stade's theorem); that ETR-INV is ∃ℝ-complete; that the guard sets of the paper's Section 5 polygon correspond exactly to the solutions of an ETR-INV instance (Theorem 54, with the range condition made explicit) and encode the solutions of any ETR formula (Theorem 55); that every real algebraic number is the x-coordinate of a guard in every optimal guard set of some polygon with rational corners (Theorem 2); and that some x-monotone polygon with integer corners can be guarded by three guards but needs four rational guards (Theorem 4). The development provides reusable material on the existential theory of the reals: formulas and their codes, the class ∃ℝ, ETR-INV and ETR-INV-REV with polynomial-time reductions from ETR, and an elementary proof of the doubly exponential solution bound that the paper cites from Schaefer and Štefankovič. It partially answers the open problem of the paper's §7.2 on the number of variables: all three art gallery problems reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards (the paper uses (n+g)^6 variables for n corners). Point-point and point-boundary hardness is proved through Stade's construction; the paper's own Section 5 construction is formalized for Theorems 54 and 55, with gadget visibility facts checked as kernel-evaluated certificates, and a modification of it (guard segments on shallow bays in the boundary, re-laid-out addition gadgets) gives boundary-point hardness. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Lean proves that deciding whether a simple polygon with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions in each of the three variants known to be ∃ℝ-complete: point guards guarding the whole polygon (Theorem 1, also for integer corners), guards on the boundary guarding the whole polygon (the boundary-point variant of the paper's §7.2), and point guards guarding only the boundary (Stade's theorem); that ETR-INV is ∃ℝ-complete; that the guard sets of the paper's Section 5 polygon correspond exactly to the solutions of an ETR-INV instance (Theorem 54, with the range condition made explicit) and encode the solutions of any ETR formula (Theorem 55); that every real algebraic number is the x-coordinate of a guard in every optimal guard set of some polygon with rational corners (Theorem 2); and that some x-monotone polygon with integer corners can be guarded by three guards but needs four rational guards (Theorem 4). The development provides reusable material on the existential theory of the reals: formulas and their codes, the class ∃ℝ, ETR-INV and ETR-INV-REV with polynomial-time reductions from ETR, and an elementary proof of the doubly exponential solution bound that the paper cites from Schaefer and Štefankovič. It partially answers the open problem of the paper's §7.2 on the number of variables: all three art gallery problems reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards (the paper uses (n+g)^6 variables for n corners). Point-point and point-boundary hardness is proved through Stade's construction; the paper's own Section 5 construction is formalized for Theorems 54 and 55, with gadget visibility facts checked as kernel-evaluated certificates, and a modification of it (guard segments on shallow bays in the boundary, re-laid-out addition gadgets) gives boundary-point hardness. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

entry.description: Agent-designed black-box algorithms with proved runtime bounds. The paper reports: The paper reports a generated black-box algorithm with expected O(n^2) runtime for its defined CycleUncover problem, where the classical(1+1) evolutionary algorithm takes exponential time, and a generated integer-valued submodular-minimization algorithm with expected O(n^(2+2c)) runtime under the stated oracle/value-range assumptions. These are mathematical algorithm/runtime constructions, not a claim that the empirical pipeline pass rate is itself a mathematical discovery. Matching known LeadingOnes bounds and generic benchmark pass rates are excluded. Direct AI involvement: Lehre directly attributes algorithm design, potential functions and drift/runtime proofs to LLM agents with Lean-filtered specifications; the paper names Claude frontier models for the completed constructions. Further checking: Check exact CycleUncover definition and black-box/oracle restrictions, the exponent parameter c and value-range assumptions in submodular minimization, and whether generated algorithms are genuinely new rather than re-encodings of known algorithms. Source code was promised for later release and was not available in the source comment; no claimed Lean proof was executed here. Exclude known-bound reproductions and incomplete pipeline fragments. Retain provisional1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed, no strict Superhuman override.

entry.description:
On the local geometry of the tight 39-point code in 𝕆P². The primary source reports: Cohn, Kumar and Minton constructed a universally optimal code of thirty-nine points in the octonionic projective plane 𝕆P², whose existence was conjectured by Hoggar. Its points form thirteen mutually unbiased Jordan frames, and a four-parameter phase family deforms the code through such configurations. This Lean development describes their local geometry under the automorphism group F₄. At every nonresonant phase, every nearby real solution of the defining equations belongs to one of four smooth families of labelled configurations. In a local slice for F₄, their union has normal form R⁴ × ⋃ᵢ₌₁⁴ R⁶ᵢ, with the R⁶ᵢ in direct sum. The distance to the localized family union is bounded by a phase-dependent constant times the square root of the residual, and the exponent 1/2 is sharp in the ambient configuration space. On an explicit open dense subset of the nonresonant phases, the complexified families are exactly the top-dimensional components of the complex solution germ, each generically reduced. Every neighbourhood of the original code in the space of unlabelled tight 39-point codes modulo F₄ contains points of local dimension 10.

The results are local, the resonant germ at the original code is not classified, and lower-dimensional complex components are not excluded. For exact frames and strongly convex C² overlap potentials, we prove a two-sided comparison of the energy gap with squared overlap errors and, near each nonresonant orbit, a quartic lower bound in distance to the localized family union. Except for attributed third-party material, all text and code are AI-generated under Robert R. MacGregor’s direction. Robert is an amateur who welcomes collaboration (macgregor@gmail.com). entry.description: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number. The primary source reports: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p. Direct AI involvement: The author chose the scope (the root count, the square-class decomposition and its corollaries, the coefficients 1, 3 and 5 in Bernoulli form, and the monic classification) and reviewed the formal statements in Challenge.lean against the paper. AI-assisted: the Lean code was drafted and repaired by Claude against the paper's statements and proofs, compiled locally with lake, and checked with Palomar's lake comparator script. The mathematics, statements and paper are the author's. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p.

entry.description: Affine profile reduction for fractional triangle packings in split graphs. The primary source reports: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main result of the author's preprint "Affine Profile Reduction for Fractional Triangle Packings in Split Graphs" (Erdős #81 series, Paper I): for every finite split graph G on n vertices, |E(G)| − 2ν₃*(G) ≤ n²/6 + n/2, where ν₃* is the fractional triangle packing number (the maximum total weight of a nonnegative weighting of the triangles with load at most one on every edge). It is stated both for the paper's finite split model (clique Fin p, independent vertices, neighbourhoods) and for every split graph in Mathlib's SimpleGraph, with the definitions of split graphs and fractional triangle packings of two registered entries; the weaker bound n²/6 + n of the first edition is also included. The proof reduces the fractional packing problem to neighbourhood profiles and a three-variable linear program, using finite LP duality. Version 2 states the finite LP duality used in the series as results of its own, over ℝ (Farkas' lemma in inequality form and covering/packing strong duality, from this proof) and over ℚ (Farkas' lemma by Fourier–Motzkin elimination and strong duality for the rational packing LP, from the author's Paper V). Direct AI involvement: AI-assisted under the author's direction and mechanically verified: no sorry, axioms limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Contributed, under the author's direction, the Lean proofs of the freeze lean_v1.2_freeze (Lean 4.28) and the API repairs of the port to Lean v4.35.0-rc3, from formal statements and proof plans.  Together with Aristotle, prepared the SimpleGraph bridge, the module-system port and the Challenge/Solution pair; wrote the packaging and checked it with a local build, a comparison of the elaborated Challenge and Solution statements and definitions (pp.all) and #print axioms (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib c55e6e786f49471c72fbddbec5415808896aec1e).  Version 2: added the rational duality modules from the author's Paper V formalization and the four duality statements to the Challenge/Solution pair; checked with a local build, a pp.all comparison of the seven Challenge/Solution declarations and #print axioms. Further checking: Only the recent split-graph bound is collected. Classical Farkas/LP duality is excluded. The mathematics is attributed to the human author; whether AI supplied material mathematics beyond formalization is unresolved.
